research_policy: Separate FSSR product identity/quality from CTR contaminants and pesticide residues. No inferred source match or active limit from generic commodity labels.

focus_8.positive_fssr_identity_quality: Acacia catechu heartwood aqueous extract; maximum total ash 8% (dry basis) and ash insoluble in HCl 0.5% (dry basis), except the specified Bhatti Katha exception.
focus_8.distinction_from_ctr: Total ash and acid-insoluble ash identity/quality criteria do not identify a CTR metal contaminant article or numerical heavy-metal limit.
focus_8.forbidden_automatic_article_transfer: Fruit, spice or coloured food contaminant entries cannot be borrowed merely because catechu is an extract or pan-masala ingredient.
proof_requirements: Supplier botanical source certificate confirming Acacia catechu heartwood and aqueous extraction.
Batch documents establishing actual dried extract and whether Bhatti Katha exception is claimed.
Quality test report for total ash and HCl-insoluble ash on the correct basis; this is not metal-limit approval.
Independently signed CTR IX finished-article and analytical-basis determination with suitable lot data.

focus_8.positive_fssr_identity_quality: Food-grade silver leaf is uniform foil with mass up to 2.8 g/m² and minimum silver fineness 999/1000; manufacture must not use animal-origin material.
focus_8.distinction_from_ctr: Silver purity and grammage are finished-product quality/identity specifications. The clause refers to CTR compliance but does not name or quantify a silver-specific contaminant limit.
focus_8.forbidden_automatic_article_transfer: Do not interpret 999/1000 silver fineness as a CTR heavy-metal PASS or the allowed concentration of lead, cadmium or arsenic.
proof_requirements: Obtain measured foil mass per square metre and material purity certificate for the actual food-grade lot.
Document no animal-origin contact during silver leaf manufacture and traceable production records.
Separate silver identity/purity checks from specific CTR contaminant analytes and their legal articles.
Obtain independent CTR IX article determination and validated final foil sample testing where applicable.

focus_8.positive_fssr_identity_quality: Carob powder is roasted pod material from Ceratonia siliqua, with total ash at most 1.2% and distinct tannin specification.
focus_8.distinction_from_ctr: The 1.2% figure is total ash for quality, not a sulphated-ash result and not a heavy-metal CTR limit.
focus_8.forbidden_automatic_article_transfer: Roasted carob is not cocoa powder, a cereal grain, nor automatically a bean/pulse analytical commodity merely because Ceratonia is in Leguminosae.
proof_requirements: Obtain the full Ceratonia siliqua roasted-pod identity and removal-of-husk production record.
Verify a traceable lot against total-ash and tannin quality standards, separately from contaminant testing.
Resolve exact legal article, source matrix and whether any CTR crop article covers this marketed pod powder.
Obtain a matrix-valid analytical method and signed regulatory classification before assigning any numeric limit.

focus_8.positive_fssr_identity_quality: Dextrin-soluble dietary fibre is dry-roasted, acidified and purified starch with average degree of polymerisation 12–25 and digestible/indigestible linkages.
focus_8.distinction_from_ctr: Degree of polymerisation and permitted use/claims are finished ingredient identity and quality facts, not CTR starch-conversion metal limits.
focus_8.forbidden_automatic_article_transfer: Starting from starch does not prove that the purified, marketed soluble fibre matches 'solid glucose and starch conversion products with sulphated ash exceeding 1.0%'.
proof_requirements: Verify the marketed dextrin source (wheat/maize), non-GM documentation and 2.11.8 identity.
Provide polymerisation/purification records and any sulphated ash result with correct analytical method.
Obtain legal interpretation excluding or applying the high-ash starch-conversion article to the exact final fibre, not its feedstock.
Obtain lot-specific metal testing after selecting the correct operative CTR article; do not infer a PASS.

focus_8.positive_fssr_identity_quality: Arrowroot is separated and purified starch from rhizomes of Maranta arundinacea or Curcuma angustifolia.
focus_8.distinction_from_ctr: A starchy-food identity is not the same as raw roots/tubers, cereal grains or milled cereal flour for CTR sampling and pesticide rules.
focus_8.forbidden_automatic_article_transfer: Do not transfer root/tuber lead or cereal-grain aflatoxin limits to isolated purified rhizome starch just because its plant source is a rhizome.
proof_requirements: Prove botanical identity and purified starch, not cassava/tapioca or raw tuber flour substitution.
Document starch extraction, washing, concentration and final moisture/sample basis.
Obtain signed current CTR article decision for purified arrowroot as marketed rather than raw root/tuber commodity.
Supply matrix-valid final starch contaminant assay only after legal limits are independently resolved.

focus_8.positive_fssr_identity_quality: Water chestnut flour is ground dried Trapa bispinosa or Trapa quadrispinosa, with moisture maximum 12%, acid-insoluble ash maximum 0.5% and a separate uric acid quality criterion.
focus_8.distinction_from_ctr: Uric acid and acid-insoluble ash in the product standard do not establish a CTR pesticide MRL, mycotoxin classification or metal limit.
focus_8.forbidden_automatic_article_transfer: The terms 'nut', 'chestnut' and 'atta' cannot automatically select CTR tree nuts, canned chestnuts or cereal-grain finished-food articles.
proof_requirements: Authenticate Trapa species, not the distinct tree-chestnut or cereal species, through supplier and product identity records.
Document dried flour manufacturing and whether any extra ingredients/additives alter final identity.
Record FSSR quality checks separately (moisture, acid-insoluble ash, uric acid).
Obtain signed determination of exact CTR mycotoxin/pesticide/metal commodity, as-sold matrix and lot data.

focus_8.positive_fssr_identity_quality: Coconut milk powder is dehydrated/spray-dried Cocos nucifera kernel-derived milk; maltodextrin and sodium caseinate may be added. Fat is at least 60% of dry mass and moisture at most 2.5%.
focus_8.distinction_from_ctr: Coconut milk powder fat and moisture specifications are quality parameters, not dairy-milk CTR lead or aflatoxin M1 limits.
focus_8.forbidden_automatic_article_transfer: The optional sodium caseinate carrier does not itself turn finished coconut powder into plain dairy milk; review allergen obligations separately.
proof_requirements: Provide actual coconut extract and optional carrier ingredients, including caseinate and maltodextrin.
Confirm spray-drying, formulation and final fat/moisture quality in the marketed product.
Obtain independent botanical-versus-dairy CTR commodity determination for final mixture and its sample basis.
Document validated as-sold contaminant testing separately, with no direct assignment of dairy milk limits.

focus_8.positive_fssr_identity_quality: Cocoa beans are properly fermented, dried whole Theobroma cacao seeds; FSSR quality includes moisture up to 8%, mouldy beans up to 4% by count, and separate damaged-bean criteria.
focus_8.distinction_from_ctr: The 4% mouldy-bean count is a physical quality acceptance criterion, NOT an aflatoxin, ochratoxin or other mycotoxin concentration limit.
focus_8.forbidden_automatic_article_transfer: Do not equate whole cocoa beans or mouldy bean count with cocoa powder's dry-fat-free lead or fat-free copper analytical basis.
proof_requirements: Trace beans as intact fermented/dried Theobroma cacao seeds rather than nibs, liquor or powder.
Check actual batch moisture, mouldy-bean count and FSSR defect specifications, separately from toxins/metals.
Obtain signed CTR IX named-article decision for whole cocoa beans and explicit correct sample/fat basis.
Verify relevant validated lot mycotoxin/metal results independently from visual mould quality status.
